name: R3M
summary: R3M pretrains a ResNet on large egocentric human video using time-contrastive learning (frames nearer in time embed nearer), video-language alignment and sparsity regularization. Frozen and handed to a behavior-cloning policy it beat ImageNet and CLIP features on manipulation, showing robot-relevant visual features should encode temporal progress and affordance rather than object category.
innovation: Time-contrastive objective capturing task progress rather than static semantics.
Established the frozen-pretrained-encoder paradigm for data-scarce robot learning.
matters: Made human video a usable pretraining corpus for manipulation before VLAs existed.
limits: Frozen features cap performance; end-to-end VLA training has largely superseded the recipe.
lineage: Visual pretraining for control, informing encoder choices in later policies.
